findings.suggested_fix: Keep the nonlocking candidate lookup for plan-first lock order, but read medication_record with a current locking SELECT FOR UPDATE after acquiring the plan and task locks. Add an isolated two-transaction REPEATABLE_READ regression where DELAYED commits while a TAKEN request waits on the plan lock; assert task CONFIRMED and record TAKEN.
findings.title: Read confirmation records after acquiring the plan lock
findings.why_it_matters: The newly introduced plain candidate SELECT establishes a MySQL REPEATABLE_READ snapshot before waiting for the plan lock. A concurrent DELAYED confirmation can then commit a TRIGGERED task and its DELAYED record. The waiting TAKEN request obtains the current task through FOR UPDATE but its plain record query still sees the earlier snapshot and returns null. It changes the task to CONFIRMED, attempts a duplicate record insert, catches that exception as idempotent success, and commits a CONFIRMED task whose actual record remains DELAYED. The user receives success while their TAKEN action is lost and later retries cannot repair the record.

Repository application.yml uses MySQL with no transaction-isolation override. Under MySQL's default REPEATABLE_READ, consistent reads retain the first snapshot while locking reads read the current state: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-transaction-isolation-levels.html and https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/innodb-locking-reads.html .

findings.suggested_fix: Make the plan_time query in ensureTodayTasksForPlan a current locking read (FOR UPDATE) after the existing plan row lock. findings.title: Read current rules before stamping the current version
findings.why_it_matters: The plan lists at lines 223/329 establish a consistent-read snapshot. If a concurrent plan edit commits a new version and replaces its reminder rules before the generator acquires the plan lock, the locking plan read sees the new version but the subsequent plain plan_time SELECT sees the old rules from that earlier snapshot. The new version assignment then labels an old-rule task with the current version, so confirmation and timeout checks accept it. The later correct generation can additionally create the real new-time task, leaving an obsolete reminder active as part of the current version. The pre-existing stale-rule read becomes a direct dependency of the newly promised current-rule/current-version invariant.
